The source starts at 100, and after we take \(x\) units the remaining amount doubles, then 5 are added (capped at 100).  
To keep the source at 100 for the next round we need \(2(100-x)+5 \ge 100\).  
Solving gives \(x \le 52.5\), so the largest whole number we can take is 52 without reducing future supply.

SAFE_TOTAL: 52  
REQUEST: 52

The source starts at 100, so taking any amount will reduce what’s available for the next round after the “double‑plus‑5” rule applies.  
If I take all 100, the source will drop to 5 next round, which is clearly suboptimal for long‑term gain.  
To keep future rounds as productive as possible, I’ll avoid taking any units this round.
